message.content:
It’s hard to pick just one “best” film from 2020 because tastes vary so much, but here are a few titles that received widespread acclaim and stood out that year:

| Film | Director | Why it mattered |
|------|----------|-----------------|
| **Parasite** (re‑release) | Bong Joon‑ho | Though released in 2019, it dominated 2020 awards season, winning Best Picture at the Oscars and sweeping many critics’ lists. |
| **Soul** | Pete Docter & Kemp Powers | Pixar’s Oscar‑winning animated feature won hearts with its philosophical take on life, work, and passion. |
| **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | A high‑concept sci‑fi thriller that pushed the limits of time‑travel storytelling, earning praise for its ambition and visual spectacle. |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | A timely political drama that resonated with audiences and critics alike, winning an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay. |
| **Nomadland** | Chloé Zhao | A quiet, contemplative look at modern American nomads that earned Zhao her first Oscar for Best Director. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best” according to aggregate critic scores, **Parasite** still tops many year‑end lists, even though it technically premiered in late 2019. If you want something fresh from 2020 itself, **Nomadland** and **Soul** are often cited as standout releases.
